flawed_step: Normality cannot be applied to C and {x} because, without the T1 assumption, {x} need not be closed.
counterexample: Let X={0,1} with topology {∅,{1},X}. Its closed sets are ∅,{0},X. It is normal: there are no two disjoint nonempty closed sets, so every disjoint pair of closed sets can be enclosed in disjoint open sets. But it is not regular. Take C={0} and x=1. Every open set containing C is X, so no open neighborhood of x can be disjoint from an open set containing C.
assessment_summary: The Sierpiński space is normal under the stated definition but fails the stated regularity condition.
